intro: A confident sigmoid can transmit almost no local gradient. Measure confidence extremes and sensitivity together.
task: Compute probabilities, mean local derivatives, and saturation fractions per unit.
requirements: logits is a batch-by-unit matrix; threshold lies strictly between 0 and 0.5. Use a numerically stable sigmoid.
Return {"probabilities": matrix, "mean_derivative": vector, "saturated_fraction": vector}. Derivative is p*(1-p); saturation means p<=threshold or p>=1-threshold, including equality.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Center and extremes
examples.output:
{'probabilities': [[0.5, 1.0], [0.5, 0.0]],
 'mean_derivative': [0.25, 0.0],
 'saturated_fraction': [0, 1]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Central unit
examples.output:
{'probabilities': [[0.5]],
 'mean_derivative': [0.25],
 'saturated_fraction': [0]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Positive threshold equality
examples.output:
{'probabilities': [[0.75]],
 'mean_derivative': [0.1875],
 'saturated_fraction': [1]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: At logit zero the probability is one half and sensitivity is maximal.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Separate positive and negative exponential formulas for extreme logits.

explanation: The derivative measures a probability’s response to a small logit change. It approaches zero when probabilities approach either endpoint, which can slow gradient transmission.
Saturation is defined here by a chosen diagnostic threshold. Its batch frequency distinguishes consistently saturated units from occasional confident responses.
